title: W1.1A VFX observational source-boundary probes
scope: Read-only application-source inspection and Node observations. Real core/FeedbackProjector/FeedbackClock plus extracted original main.ts functions at explicitly mocked presentation boundaries. NOT a browser, WebGL, animation-rendering, FPS, GPU-disposal or physical-device test.
acceptanceMeaning: Exit 0 only means observations were collected. This script does not assert the defects are fixed and does not turn old defective outputs into passing acceptance results.
mockedBoundaries: world calls use the real FeedbackClock instead of a renderer
audio play requests counted, no audio device used

observations.description: A live commit completes after the page-hidden cancellation.
observations.originalObservation: A sale transient is active and one sound playback is requested while hidden.
observations.intendedRepair: Consume the committed event without starting transient FX/audio while hidden; preserve any useful aggregate result separately.

observations.description: The UI wall-clock reveal timer ends before the clamped scene clock.
observations.originalObservation: UI reveal/Skip flag is false while the reveal clock remains active at 600/1100 ms.
observations.intendedRepair: Keep the Skip control and scene completion on the same presentation lifecycle, or explicitly finish/cancel the scene when the UI timer expires.

observations.description: Current selection changes while a display command is awaiting commit.
observations.indices: Zero-based: actual shelf 1 means player-facing shelf 2; current selection 2 means player-facing shelf 3.
observations.originalObservation: The committed shelf is index 1, but the feedback target is index 2.
observations.intendedRepair: Use the immutable target captured for the successful display command or derive the intended committed target, rather than the later UI selection.

limitations: F1 models the exact ordering of hidden cancellation then successful in-flight commit; it does not measure real IDB race frequency.
F2 simulates 100 ms frame intervals and invokes the actual recorded UI callback; it does not claim a measured device frame rate.
F3 verifies the actual projector target argument mismatch; it does not claim a rendered shelf animation was observed.
Application source, normal/sandbox user saves and the production Site are not modified.
